patch.value: Release workflow pushed version bump straight to protected main, killing the job before the tag push

The release workflow ended with Push release tag and main which ran git push origin HEAD:main before git push origin for the tag. main is protected across the fleet (required checks, enforce_admins, required_conversation_resolution), so the push to main was rejected with GH006 and set -e killed the job before the tag push, causing every daily release in the fleet to fail on 2026-08-10. The fix ports the protected-PR merge pattern from pm-beads: the version bump is merged through a release PR via the GitHub merge API, then the tag is pushed only after the merge is verified, so git push origin HEAD:main never appears again.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Fixed in .github/workflows/release.yml: replaced the Push release tag and main step with a protected-PR merge (Merge release metadata through protected PR), a Verify merged release step that asserts the merged SHA and the Cargo-form crate version, and a Push release tag step that tags only. The merge loop resolves unresolved review threads via GraphQL resolveReviewThread, attempts the merge API with merge_method=rebase, detects action_required CI runs, and never polls mergeStateStatus to decide the merge. permissions now include pull-requests: write and actions: write.

value.author: claude
value.text: Round two review fix. The Push release tag step consulted only the local tag database while the last tag fetch happens in Decide release, so a tag created on origin in between would be missed, git tag would succeed locally and the push would be rejected as non-fast-forward. It now fetches tags and compares against the remote tag target. The dist rebuild check does not apply here because pm-rust is a Cargo package with no tracked dist directory.

value.author: claude
value.text: CodeRabbit found a security regression in the thread resolution I added. The loop resolved every unresolved review thread on the release pull request, which would also clear a human reviewer's blocking thread and remove exactly the protection required_conversation_resolution provides for release commits. The GraphQL query now selects the first comment's author type and only bot authored threads are resolved. The jq filter was verified against a sample payload containing one bot thread and one human thread, and it returned only the bot thread.

value.author: claude
value.text: Round four review fixes. Greptile found that classifying a review thread by its first comment lets a bot opened thread with a substantive human reply be auto resolved, which bypasses the human concern entirely. A thread now counts as advisory only when every comment on it is bot authored, and an empty comment list is excluded. The filter was verified against four thread shapes, all bot, mixed bot then human, human only, and empty, and it selects only the all bot thread. CodeRabbit found that the dist rebuild check omitted ignored matching, so newly generated ignored files under dist would stay hidden and a stale or orphaned artifact could still ship.

value.author: claude
value.text: Round five review fix. Greptile found that fetching only the first hundred thread comments lets a human reply past that page escape the all bot predicate, so the filter now refuses to resolve any thread whose comment total exceeds the comments actually returned. The dist rebuild check does not apply here because pm-rust is a Cargo package with no tracked dist directory.
